new.name: APPLIES_STATED_CONSTRAINT_TO_DESIGN
new.definition: The reasoning cites a requirement or constraint taken from the task specification and uses it to justify, validate, or rule out a proposed technical approach.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text that links a task constraint to a candidate technical approach.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning identifies a specific requirement or constraint stated in the task.
The reasoning connects that requirement to a concrete candidate approach or configuration choice.
The reasoning states whether the proposed approach satisfies the cited constraint.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning merely lists or restates requirements without connecting them to any approach.
The cited constraint plays no role in judging or selecting the approach.
The reasoning evaluates an approach only on grounds unrelated to any stated requirement.

new.name: SELECTS_APPROACH_FROM_CONSIDERED_ALTERNATIVES
new.definition: The reasoning explicitly weighs two or more alternative ways of achieving the same goal and commits to one of them with an articulated rationale.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text comparing candidate approaches and stating the chosen one.

assertion_conditions: At least two distinct candidate approaches are identified for the same goal.
The reasoning states a comparison or trade-off between them.
The reasoning explicitly commits to one approach and gives a reason for the choice.
exclusion_conditions: Only a single approach is described with no alternative considered.
Alternatives are mentioned but no selection is made.
The reasoning restates a chosen approach without comparing it to any alternative.

new.name: RECOGNIZES_ANOMALY_IN_OBSERVATION
new.definition: The reasoning identifies a condition in an observation as unexpected, unplanned, or interfering, and treats it as something requiring explanation or handling.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The reasoning that flags the reported condition as unexpected and states its significance.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The observation reporting the unexpected condition, conflict, or deviation.

assertion_conditions: The observation reports a warning, conflict, deviation, or otherwise unanticipated condition.
The reasoning characterizes that condition as unexpected, contradictory, or requiring investigation.
The reasoning states why the condition matters for the intended outcome.
exclusion_conditions: The observation matches the expected outcome and the reasoning treats it as normal success.
The reasoning merely quotes the reported condition without judging it unexpected.
The deviation is only inferred later without the reasoning connecting it to the observation.

new.name: VERIFIES_INTENDED_STATE_WITH_CHECK
new.definition: An action includes an explicit check of an operational state whose reported result is used to confirm that an intended state was actually reached after setup or change actions were performed.

parameters.name: check_action
parameters.description: The action that performs or embeds the state check on the just-established configuration.

parameters.name: intent_reasoning
parameters.description: The reasoning stating the intended state that must be achieved and confirmed.

parameters.name: check_observation
parameters.description: The observation reporting the checked state, confirming or contradicting the intended state.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning states the operational state that the setup is intended to produce or that must be validated.
The action performs a state check covering that intended condition.
The observation reports a directly interpretable outcome of the check for that condition.
exclusion_conditions: The query examines pre-existing state before any relevant change was made.
The observation contains no interpretable evidence about the intended state.
Only a validation of syntax or intent is stated without any check result.

new.name: RETRIES_WITH_CORRECTED_ACTION
new.definition: After an invocation fails and its error is observed, a follow-up action repeats the same intent while repairing the specific defect reported by the error.

parameters.name: failed_action
parameters.description: The invocation that failed and produced the error.

parameters.name: failure_observation
parameters.description: The observation reporting the failure of that invocation.

parameters.name: corrected_action
parameters.description: The subsequent invocation pursuing the same goal with the reported defect fixed.

assertion_conditions: The first action fails and an observation reports the failure.
The subsequent action pursues the same goal as the failed action.
The subsequent action differs in the respect identified by the error, removing the defect.
exclusion_conditions: The retry repeats the invocation unchanged after the error.
The subsequent action pursues a different goal rather than retrying.
No error observation exists to motivate the correction.

uncertain.name: PERFORMS_PRECEDING_RECONNAISSANCE
uncertain.definition: A read-only action gathers information about the current environment because the reasoning declares that the existing state must be known before any modification is attempted.

parameters.name: reconnaissance_action
parameters.description: The action that only inspects or queries existing system state.

parameters.name: plan_reasoning
parameters.description: The reasoning expressing the intent to inspect the current state before making changes.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning states that the current state, configuration, or available tooling must be inspected before modifications.
The action collects existing state without altering it.
The resulting information constitutes the basis for the subsequent setup steps.
exclusion_conditions: The read-only query checks whether a change already made took effect.
No inspection-first intent is expressed in the reasoning.
The action changes system state rather than only reading it.
